title: The 2009 Flickr Talk That Named the DevOps Movement
explainer: At the Velocity conference in June 2009, Flickr engineers John Allspaw and Paul Hammond gave a talk called '10+ Deploys Per Day: Dev and Ops Cooperation at Flickr,' describing how automated infrastructure, shared version control, and one-step build-and-deploy let them ship many times a day instead of in rare, risky batches. The talk is widely credited as a founding moment of the DevOps movement, and the frequent, low-drama deploy pipeline it describes is essentially what a CI/CD tool like GitHub Actions automates for you today.
